entries.label: SQL Server connector and dependency security

sections.title: Added
items: Added an isolated SQL Server connector with direct TCP SQL authentication, verified TLS and private-CA support; no SSH or Windows-side gateway agent is required.
SQL Server reuses the shared SQL console, schema browser, autocomplete, sessions and result exports. Five read-only actions use the existing permission, approval, history, audit and MCP pipeline.
Added full-grammar, fail-closed T-SQL read validation and a disposable SQL Server 2022 fixture covering TLS, cancellation, writable-canary policy regressions, exact scalar values and result limits.

SQL Server checks supported result types before query execution, preserves timezone-free date/time semantics, and requires a submitted password when changing a profile username. Shared SQL completion preserves escaped identifiers and supports quoted Enter/Tab acceptance.

sections.title: Security
items: Updated golang.org/x/net to 0.62.0 for GO-2026-6860 in Mail HTML parsing, with a bounded allocation regression for ignored-tag text coalescing.
Updated the MCP SDK's transitive Hono Node adapter to 2.1.6 for GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f; an encoded-path regression fails against the vulnerable dependency. The bridge remains stdio-only.
The frontend runtime explicitly requires libexpat 2.10.0-r0 or later for CVE-2026-117610 and CVE-2026-118370; a fresh image scan found the older package in a cached layer.

SQL Server execution uses checked platform-width integer conversions for ports and row limits, with invalid-range and 32-bit boundary regressions; malformed query plans fail before opening a connection.

Patched Kafka's klauspost/compress dependency to 1.20.3 for GHSA-fpmh-frq8-7rj8. A regression reproduces the prior two-block zstd panic through the actual bounded decompressor and retains normal decoding and size-limit checks.
The unprivileged frontend image requires curl and libcurl 8.23.0-r0 or later for CVE-2026-92392 while retaining the stable nginx 1.30.6 base.
Updated development-only Vite to 6.4.5; a real loopback server regression checks filesystem denial with transform-query suffixes.

sections.title: Maintenance
items: Refreshed the Go 1.27.3 builder image digest together with the native dependency inventory, frontend Lucide/jscpd patches, and immutable CodeQL 4.39.1 action pins.

Aligned contributor, CI and frontend builder Node.js pins at 24.22.2, and updated MCP SDK 1.32.2, ClickHouse driver 2.50.0, React Router 8.5.1, Lucide 1.65.0, TypeScript ESLint 8.72.1 and fake-indexeddb 6.2.7 through maintainer-authored commits.
SQL Server cancellation conformance observes an explicit fixture-only exclusive table lock and a blocked SELECT before cancellation, rather than assuming a no-op update holds the required lock.
Reviewed dependency license identities retain unchanged Go evidence and acknowledged historical gaps. Existing quality and verification budgets remain enforced.

sections.title: Notes
items: The SQL Server connector is read-only: stored procedures, write SQL, managed users and backup/restore are not included. Use least-privilege database credentials. No database migration or new MCP tool family is introduced.

AIPermission remains local-only and single-user. Back up the encrypted database before upgrading; publish the MCP package separately. Conformance uses SQL Server 2022 on Linux, not a certification of every Windows server configuration.

Development-only minimatch consumers retain a moderate amplification advisory pending compatible upstream updates. Production npm audits pass; existing SQLCipher native-update limitations remain documented.

entries.label: Connector boundary and credential lifecycle hardening

sections.title: Security
items: Kubernetes resource descriptions mask inline environment values and embedded last-applied manifests; logs and arbitrary application fields still require operator care.
Postgres managed roles use client-derived SCRAM-SHA-256 verifiers instead of plaintext passwords in role statements. Newly managed roles require SCRAM-capable clients.
Setup and unlock classify known validation and recovery errors while withholding unexpected internal failure details.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Best-effort manual console capture distinguishes real heredocs from shifts, quoted operators and here-strings; regression tests cover literal delimiters, compound statements, body omission and subsequent history resumption.
ClickHouse metadata identifiers and remote filesystem paths retain exact identity through preparation and execution; malformed transfer path arrays are rejected.
Typed REST responses enforce published inclusive integer bounds without losing int64 precision.
Credential editors can explicitly remove optional S3 session tokens and Redis passwords; leaving a secret blank still preserves its stored value.

sections.title: Maintenance
items: Added atomic read-triggered Vault expiry audit tests, bounded diagnostics for all conformance fixtures, role-history scaling measurements, and corrected MCP replay and configurable migration-port guidance.
Settings and storage documentation clarify that changing the active database password does not re-encrypt existing snapshots or remote backups.

sections.title: Notes
items: AIPermission remains local-only, single-user and developer-focused. No new connector or database schema migration is introduced; back up the encrypted database before upgrading.

Full role-history inspection remains a measured scalability limitation, not a bounded-scan implementation. Previously documented SQLCipher native limitations remain unchanged; this release does not update the cipher.
The MCP package must be published separately after the GitHub release.

entries.label: Patched runtimes and MCP dependency security

sections.title: Security
items: MCP requires patched Node.js release lines: 22.23.4+, 24.22.1+, or 26.12.1+; unsupported runtimes fail before gateway access. Contributor, CI and builder pins use Node.js 24.22.1.
The unprivileged frontend runtime pins nginx 1.30.6 for CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-93479 and CVE-2026-97205, and requires native Brotli 1.2.1-r0 for CVE-2026-111497.
MCP uses patched Zod 4.6.7 with failure-first gateway validation and record schemas compatible with the SDK. The frontend's development-only Zod copy is aligned.

Patched the SDK dependency tree's body-parser to 2.4.0, fast-uri to 3.1.9 and ip-address to 10.7.4. Isolated regressions cover decoder teardown, URI ambiguity and oversized IPv6 zone input without adding an HTTP server to the stdio bridge.

sections.title: Maintenance
items: Reviewed frontend router/icon and MCP ESLint/TypeScript ESLint metadata updates retain the dependency license inventory and maintainer-authored history.
Added encrypted storage boundary tests for URI-option-looking filenames and passwords, adversarial snapshot names, exact-password reopen and rekey isolation.

sections.title: Notes
items: Upgrade the Node.js interpreter used by your MCP client before installing this package, then restart the client. An already running client does not adopt a newly installed interpreter automatically.

SQLCipher remains 4.16.0: the selected wrapper has no published patched artifact. Two known native fixes are not reachable through current application APIs; application-boundary tests are not a native patch. The upstream update remains explicitly tracked in the native dependency documentation.
AIPermission remains local-only, single-user and developer-focused. No connector, database schema migration or permission change is introduced. Back up the encrypted database before upgrading.
The MCP package must be published separately after the GitHub release.

sections.title: Security
items: The frontend runtime requires libX11 1.8.14-r0 or later for CVE-2026-88806, retaining existing PCRE2/TIFF guards and the unprivileged runtime user.
DOMPurify is pinned to 3.4.17; Monaco's production and development sanitizer replacement remains enforced.
Go 1.27.3 includes the upstream crypto/x509 security mitigation for CVE-2026-111943.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Deferred transfer recovery assertions use explicit synchronization so a successful asynchronous retry cannot produce a false shutdown-order failure.
Architecture verification avoids repeated allocating inventory scans and reuses context-scoped detached snapshots without dropping platform, fixture or security checks.
The editor optimizer regression reads the exact sanitizer version from the package manifest instead of rejecting a valid reviewed patch update.

sections.title: Maintenance
items: Coordinated Go 1.27.3 and Node.js 24.22.0 across contributor setup, CI, Docker builders and native dependency metadata.
Updated Kafka kmsg to 1.15.0, React to 19.3.1, dialog and icon dependencies, Playwright to 1.64.1, Vitest to 4.1.12 and Prettier to 3.9.10 with reviewed license metadata.
Pinned Linux workflows to Ubuntu 24.04 and updated both CodeQL analyses to immutable 4.39.0 action references.
Documented live repository protection checks and the private vulnerability reporting channel; bot dependency proposals are replaced by maintainer-authored commits.

sections.title: Notes
items: AIPermission remains local-only, single-user and developer-focused; connector isolation, token permissions, Always grants and finite resource limits are unchanged.
Back up the encrypted database before upgrading. No database schema migration or new connector is introduced.
The MCP package must be published separately after the GitHub release.

entries.label: Mail ownership and dependency security hardening

sections.title: Security
items: SMTP PLAIN authentication registers its reusable wire credential for mandatory masking, including reflected authentication errors and optional-redaction-off mode.
Postgres bounds incoming protocol message bodies to 4 MiB during startup and query execution, independently of the returned-output budget.

Maintenance console startup requires procfs in the current PID namespace; teardown continues cleaning validated descendants when unrelated process metadata is unavailable, sends final signals after slow validation and reports incomplete verification.
Coordinated Go 1.26.9 compiler, CI and container pins with golang.org/x/net 0.61.0 and its required crypto, sys and text updates address newly reported standard-library and HTTP/2 advisories.
The frontend runtime requires TIFF 4.7.2-r0 or later to address CVE-2026-4775 while retaining the patched PCRE2 minimum and unprivileged runtime user.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Mail outbound actions retain uncertain and pending request ownership across drafts and remounts until exact reconciliation; canceled in-flight replies retain their source message and subsequent uncertain sends retain their own message identity.
Definitive local mail dispatch failures are distinguished from uncertain remote outcomes without enabling automatic resend.
S3 uploads accept explicitly empty text or Base64 content through the generic action schema while preserving single-content-field validation and overwrite preconditions.

sections.title: Maintenance
items: Date conversion tests exercise UTC, Istanbul and Los Angeles without relying on the contributor's timezone.
The documented Linux amd64 backend test image includes checksum-pinned kubectl without adding it to the production image.
Contributor documentation distinguishes authorized action execution from scoped credential management capabilities.
Updated MCP SDK to 1.32.1, smol-toml to 1.9.1, frontend dialog/icon dependencies, Playwright to 1.64.0, Vite to 6.4.4 and related lint/duplication tooling with reviewed license metadata.
Updated immutable GitHub Actions pins for setup-node 7.1.0 and CodeQL 4.38.3.

sections.title: Notes

entries.label: Connector identity and request ownership hardening

sections.title: Security
items: MCP config updates retain private recovery snapshots, detect conflicting writers and reject tracked recovery paths, including case variants; filesystem limitations remain explicit.
MCP structural dispatch identifiers are canonicalized while exact response identity checks and opaque action inputs remain unchanged.
Redis query changes and refresh retire stale confirmations and UI results without canceling an already dispatched mutation.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Kafka preserves exact consumer group identities, including whitespace, and reports payload bytes only for returned records.
Redis scan cursors, results and selections belong to their applied query; backup provider collections reject stale replies across refresh and workspace changes.
RabbitMQ binary previews enforce decoded-byte limits and preserve valid Base64; text previews retain valid UTF-8 boundaries.
Unknown SMTP submission outcomes use the canonical dispatch-stage and reconciliation metadata without automatic retry.

sections.title: Maintenance
items: The npm placeholder ships the AGPL license with package-content verification.
Packaged MCP stdio behavior is exercised on the minimum Node.js 20.0.0 runtime on Linux x64; maintained Node.js releases remain recommended.
Credential documentation distinguishes mandatory registered-secret masking from best-effort handling of unrelated or transformed data.

sections.title: Notes
items: AIPermission remains local-only, single-user and developer-focused; permissions, Always grants and finite resource limits are unchanged.
Back up the encrypted database before upgrading. No new database schema migration is introduced.

Config recovery is not a portable filesystem compare-and-swap guarantee; review retained snapshots before removing them. Windows filesystems without hard links reject first-time credential config creation with recovery guidance.
The MCP package must be published separately after the GitHub release.

sections.title: Security
items: Postgres restore artifacts stay within gateway restricted mode; backup execution selects a client matching the server major version.
MCP secret input detaches terminal echo before reading credentials, and frontend reads reject cross-workspace responses before applying data.
SSH directory metadata is bounded before accumulation, preserving finite resource limits.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Console transcript tail reconstruction follows actual UTF-8 byte boundaries.
Postgres read-only validation distinguishes boolean grouping from function calls without broadening the allowed function policy.
Postgres Console discovers tables through get_tables and lazily loads ordered columns through describe_table, including across new sessions and retained SQL drafts.
Automatic retention cleanup records its audit atomically with the cleanup transaction.
New database password length is measured in Unicode code points; existing passwords remain unchanged.
MCP doctor recognizes the exact Windows npx launcher.

sections.title: Maintenance
items: Kubernetes documentation clarifies that autonomous restart grants are optional and remain explicitly operator-controlled.
Behavioral regressions cover credential input, workspace identity, transcript reconstruction, bounded metadata, SQL validation, retention and console metadata ownership.

sections.title: Notes
items: AIPermission remains local-only, single-user and developer-focused; connector permission and approval policies are unchanged.
Back up the encrypted database before upgrading. This release adds no database schema migration.
The MCP package must be published separately after the GitHub release.

entries.label: Connector capacity visibility and storage recovery

sections.title: Added
items: Settings displays per-token retained request bytes, records, result reservations, running requests and pending approvals, with storage warnings at 80% and 90% and explicit exhaustion guidance.
An authenticated local-only capacity report exposes configured limits and history retention without returning token values, credentials, commands or request payloads.
The operator-owned AIPERMISSION_CONNECTOR_REQUEST_STORAGE_MIB setting accepts integer budgets from 256 to 4096 MiB; the default remains 256 MiB and invalid configuration prevents startup.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Persisted request storage exhaustion reports a stable limit reason and safe token-scoped usage instead of suggesting that waiting 60 seconds always restores capacity; concurrency exhaustion retains retry guidance.
Capacity polling has a bounded deadline, ignores stale completions, clears cached token identities after UI session invalidation and explicitly marks failed refreshes as stale.

sections.title: Changed
items: Schema migration 43 installs a compact numeric request-usage projection maintained atomically by canonical writes, rollback and retention, avoiding repeated aggregation of retained request payloads without duplicating secret content.
Storage accounting preserves UTF-8 byte sizes, active result reservations, atomic admission, idempotent replay and existing row and concurrency limits.

sections.title: Notes
items: Back up the encrypted database before upgrading. Migration runs on unlock; rolling back to an older binary requires restoring the pre-upgrade database rather than opening schema 43 with that binary.
Larger finite budgets can still fill. Review retention and disk capacity; this release does not silently erase recent history, increase limits automatically or change connector permissions.
AIPermission remains local-only, single-user and developer-focused. The MCP package must be published separately after the GitHub release.
